clauses.title: Scope – Covers types
clauses.text: 1. Scope -  Covers types of plywood with ornamental veneers on one or both faces used for decorative purposes, such as furniture making, panelling of all kinds, including panelling for railway coaches, buses and ships.

clauses.title: Determine decrotave plywood shall
clauses.text: 2.1  Determine decrotave plywood shall be of two grades, namely BWR and MR

clauses.title: Decorative plywood shall be
clauses.text: 2.2  Decorative plywood shall be of two types, namely Type 1 and Type 2

clauses.title: Materials – The species
clauses.text: 3. Materials - The species of timber commonly used for decorative veneers  or  decorative plywood  shall be specified by the purchaser. Commonly used species are given in Annex. B of the standard. Any species of timber may be used for cores and backs of decorative veneered plywood. However, a list of species, given in Annex B of  IS 303 : 1989* may be used for guidance The adhesive for bonding of veneers shall be MR and BWR type synthetic resin adhesive, conforming to IS 848: 1974.+ for MR  and BWR grade veneered decorative ply respectively. Plywood, when used in the manufacture of veneered decorative plywood of MR and BWR  grade  shall be MR  and BWR type conforming to IS 303 : 1989.*

clauses.title: Type 1
clauses.text: 4.1 Type 1—Open splits, checks or open Joints not more than 150 mm in length and 0.5 mm in width shall be permissible provided the same are rectified with a veneer insert bonded with synthetic resin adhesive. Shall be free from torn grain, dead knots, dote, discolouration and sapwood.The decorative veneered surface shall be selected for figure, texture, colour and grain characteristics. It shall be free from all manufacturing and wood defects except to the extent permitted above.

clauses.title: Type 2
clauses.text: 4.2 Type 2 — Open splits, checks, or open joints not more than 200 mm in length and 1 mm in width shall be permissible, provided these are rectified in the manner specified under 4.1. Tight knots and patches not more than 25 mm in diameter, and pin knots not more than 4 mm in diameter, shall be permissible.

clauses.title: Shall be free from
clauses.text: 4.2.1 Shall be free from the torn grain, dead knots, dote and discolouration. Sapwood, if it does not affect the appearance, shall be permissible.

clauses.title: Surface shall be selected
clauses.text: 4.2.2 Surface shall be selected for figure, texture, colour and grain characteristics. It shall be free from all manufacturing and wood defects, except to the extent permitted above.

clauses.title: The dimensions and tolerances (including on
clauses.text: 5.1 The dimensions and tolerances (including on thickness ) of plywood  shall be as given in IS 12049 : 1987 ++. Note -  Any other dimension as agreed to between the manufacture and for chaser may be used

clauses.title: Thickness
clauses.text: 5.2 Thickness — Thickness of the plywood boards shall be 3 mm, 4 mm, 6 mm, 9 mm,12 mm, 19 mm or 25 mm.

clauses.title: Tests
clauses.text: 6. Tests a) Moisture content — Not less than 5 percent and more than15 percent. b) Water resistance test—Shall not show delamination or blister formation when tested as per the standard.

clauses.title: Finish
clauses.text: 7. Finish —The edges of the decorative plywood shall be trimmed square within 3 mm and sanded to a smooth finish. ++Dimensions and  tolerances relating  to wood based panel materials. Note—For method of tests, refer to the standard and IS 1734 (Part 1) : 1983 Method of tests for plywood, Part1 determination of density and moisture(second revision). For detailed Information, refer to  IS  1328 : 1996  Specification for veneered decorative plywood  (third revision). * Plywood for general purpose (first revision) + Synthetic resin adhesive for plywood (phenolic and aminoplastic) (first revision)
